messages:
incident-bot: PAGE: capacity-tier-routing-errors — 75% of fallback requests are returning hosted pool endpoints for tenants bound to Dedicated pools. Escalation level: P1. Auto-attach runbook: capacity-tier-fallback.

ops-jordan: saw the bot — oncall-sre, can you take? customer reports latency spikes and auth failures. @oncall-sre

oncall-sre: taking. currently seeing ~1.1k misrouted requests/min for the dedicated-tenants prefix. Marking incidented. Running initial impact check.

eng-routing: quick note — we're seeing fallback routing policy choose the hosted fallback variant (model: redwood-small-hosted) instead of the dedicated-compatible variant (redwood-small-dedicated). Probable mis-eval in policy precedence after the rollout earlier today.

infra-lydia: logs look like this from router-proxy (trimmed):
```
2026-03-15T09:14:02Z router-proxy route_eval: tenant=acme-co policy=route_fallback priority=10 selected=hosted_pool id=hp-42
2026-03-15T09:14:02Z router-proxy bind_attempt: pool=dedicated-acme-1 match=false reason=variant_mismatch
2026-03-15T09:14:03Z tracer: kvcache_hit=false batching=small seq=1
```

ops-jordan: customer-impact: CS reported 3 enterprise customers (acme-co, hardy-labs, bluefirm) saw ~20-40% error rates and large latency increases between 09:10-09:40 UTC. They're seeing model mismatch errors in app logs (expected private variant, got hosted).

customer-success: contacted acme-co (account manager on call). They confirmed requests returned 403/variant-mismatch for some calls, and flagged sensitive prompt rejection when hitting hosted endpoint. They're being paged and want ETA.

oncall-sre: immediate mitigation plan — 1) disable fallback to hosted for tenants with dedicated binding (fast config flip), 2) add temporary route-mask to force dedicated-pref on policy engine, 3) increase dedicated pool capacity if eviction is happening. Executing step 1 now.

eng-routing: hold — before flip, the rollout that changed precedence added an allowlist for region fallback. It appears the new precedence rule sets `fallback.preference = hosted` for global path; dedicated match had lower weight. PR: https://git.internal/redwood/routing/pulls/2246 (merged 08:50 UTC).

sre-alex: confirming — I can revert the merge or patch the weights. Reverting is fastest. Preparing revert PR.

infra-lydia: applying emergency policy patch to edge: `rctl policy set fallback.preference=dedicated --scope=tenant-bound` (dry-run then apply). Running dry-run now.

eng-routing: dry-run result: would re-route 14k requests over next 10m back to dedicated pools. Risk: dedicated pools currently at 85% mem utilization; may see queueing. Suggest also enabling short-term throttle on incoming traffic to reduce burst.

oncall-sre: proceed with applying patch and enact throttling. Applying patch in 30s. Will monitor CPU/GPU queue and error rate metrics.

ops-jordan: posting mitigation commands for on-call (for audit):
```
# force dedicated preference for tenant-bound requests
rctl policy patch --name capacity-tier-fallback --set "fallback.preference=dedicated" --filter "tenant_bound==true" --author oncall-sre
# apply short-term ingress throttle
kubectl -n router set configmap ingress-throttle --from-literal=rate=5000r/s
```

oncall-sre: patch applied at 09:23:04 UTC. Ingress throttle applied at 09:23:20 UTC. Monitoring...

incident-bot: metric update: wrong-route-count: 1100 -> 120 -> 15 (09:24 -> 09:30 -> 09:36). latency-95 reduced from 1.8s -> 0.9s for affected tenants.

customer-success: acme-co says errors dropped to ~2% and latency improving, thanks. They're still concerned about data twice-hitting hosted endpoints earlier — CS suggests a follow-up runbook and transparency note.

eng-routing: root cause summary (prelim): accidental precedence inversion introduced in PR 2246 where `global_fallback.preference` shadowed `tenant_binding.preference` due to policy evaluation ordering change. The policy engine now resolves the global key last, overriding tenant-bound choices. This wasn't covered by tests because the test harness only exercised single-key evaluation.

infra-lydia: additional telemetry finding — we saw a region fallback loop starting for eu-west: some requests were rerouted eu-west -> us-east (hosted) -> eu-west (dedicated) when policies re-evaluated after failure, creating churn and overload on connectors. Loop retries contributed ~18% extra load.

oncall-sre: mitigation step 2: add loop-protection flag `policy.loop_guard=true` and set max_retries=1. Patching now.

ops-jordan: applied loop guard at 09:28:50 UTC. Loop retries dropped to 0 in the next minute.

eng-routing: long-term remediations: 1) update policy engine to evaluate tenant-scoped keys with higher precedence and add unit tests for multi-key precedence, 2) add synthetic tests that exercise fallback combos including dedicated/hosted/region, 3) add canary gating on precedence-changing PRs. Creating tickets: RG-1240, RG-1241, RG-1242.

product-ops: request to draft customer-facing incident summary and timeline. We should include affected tenants, mitigation steps, and what we're doing to prevent recurrence. CS to coordinate.

customer-success: will compile impacted account list and send proactive notifications this morning. Will also open support cases for any customers who saw data policy exposure.

oncall-sre: handoff note for next on-call: incident remains in monitoring state, wrong-route-count stable at ~0-3/min. Dedicated pool utilization at 72%. Action items for follow-up: verify PR 2246 revert merged and hotfix tests added; confirm no residual logs referencing hosted endpoints for dedicated tenants; postmortem owner: eng-routing.

sre-alex: revert PR merged at 09:45 UTC (revert 2250). Running CI for hotfix.

incident-bot: incident transitioned to MONITOR at 10:00 UTC. Pager resolved.

ops-jordan: tagging postmortem and assigning to eng-routing. Will create a high-level executive note and include CS summary.

eng-routing: acknowledged. I'll take postmortem and work with infra to harden the policy engine. Thanks to everyone for the fast mitigation. :heart:
